competitors.name: Yough!
competitors.action: Yough's Greek-yogurt frozen pizzas expanded into nearly 2,000 Target stores, pushing a high-protein pizza format that delivers roughly 40g-50g protein per pizza and gives the frozen aisle a stronger functional-nutrition angle.

competitors.name: Di Fara
competitors.action: Di Fara is expanding its frozen pizza line with a new Three-Meat pie priced under $10 and is reportedly looking to grow into chains like Kroger and Lidl, signaling that well-known independent pizzerias are still moving into grocery with premium credibility plus sharper value pricing.

competitors.name: RAGÚ x Palermo Villa
competitors.action: RAGÚ's collaboration with Palermo Villa extended a legacy sauce brand into frozen pizza, showing the at-home pizza occasion is broadening beyond standalone pizza brands into cross-category CPG partnerships that can win on familiarity and retailer trust.

trends.topic: Frozen pizza innovation is splitting into two winning lanes: functional nutrition and restaurant-backed authenticity
trends.magnitude: Target-scale distribution for protein-forward Yough and continued grocery expansion from Di Fara both surfaced in the latest scan
trends.context: The category is not moving in one direction. One lane is macro-driven and nutrition-forward, while the other is chef- or restaurant-led and quality-forward. Real Dough sits much closer to the authenticity lane, but the nutrition lane matters because it is teaching retailers to look for a sharper product story than generic premium claims.

breaking.headline: Target-scale and grocery-chain expansion signals the freezer aisle still has room for differentiated pizza stories
breaking.impact: Real Dough should keep sharpening a single, obvious reason to win at shelf, ideally rooted in crust and restaurant-grade credibility, because both high-protein challengers and independent pizzeria brands are earning space with much clearer hooks than generic premium positioning.
